title: WSPR Band-Opening Time-of-Day Map
dataSources: APRS packets (`aprs:packet`), WSPR spots (`wspr:spot`), satellite passes (`satpass:prediction`), NOAA APT captures (`noaa:apt`), meteor-scatter pings (`meteorscatter:ping`), SSTV images (`sstv:image`).
app: Software-defined radio and ham-radio stations — APRS igate, WSPR beacon, NOAA weather-satellite (APT) receiver, meteor-scatter monitor, and SSTV decoder — logging to Splunk HEC via scripted inputs.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=wspr:spot
| eval hour=strftime(_time,"%H")
| stats avg(distance_km) as reach by band hour
| sort band hour
description: Maps when each radio band tends to open for long distance by hour, guiding when to listen for far-away signals.
value: Band openings follow the sun; charting reach by hour and band turns propagation folklore into your own measured schedule.
implementation: Ingest WSPR spots with timestamps; review average reach by band and hour to learn your local openings.
visualization: Heatmap of average reach by band and hour of day.
grandmaExplanation: It shows what times of day each radio band carries signals furthest, so you know when to listen.
